BiblicalUsage: Peithos means persuasive, enticing — the kind of speech that wins by cleverness. Paul says his preaching was not with enticing words of man's wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that a sermon proved by the Spirit outlasts a speech proved by cleverness, and I would rather have power than polish.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
